title: Vol structures
dek: Inner vol book: five standing Brent options trades, the capped-grinder candidate structures, the house view expressed as trades, a candidate put spread, and the pre-committed strike plan. For each trade: what happens if Brent moves $1, what time passing does, what fear does, and the most it can lose.

claims.text: At the October 23, 2026 ICE Brent settlements (January 2027 expiry, futures 111.70), the five standing vol structures mark: own the tail premium paid 2.41 per barrel, call spread paid 2.07, fade the wing collected 0.32, risk reversal collected 0.09, covered call collected 3.08. The covered call collects $105 per lot per day in rent (theta) at those marks.

What a $1 Brent rise does at the same marks, per 1,000-barrel lot: covered call gains about $746, tail call gains about $206, risk reversal gains about $506. If fear jumps one point, the tail call gains about $97.

Candidate structures at the same marks, tracked, not corpus plays: the lopsided condor collects collected 3.56 per barrel with the most it can lose at $11,440 per lot; the capped straddle collects collected 10.56 per barrel, about three times the condor's rent, worst case $5,940 per lot; the capped risk reversal cuts S4's crash loss from $100,910 to $11,960 per lot.

House view dated October 25, 2026, rendered on this page as expressions: S3 call-spread fade (the grinder), S5 covered overwrite, S1 and S2 as the convex side, and a wingy put spread marked CANDIDATE (unnumbered, not in the tracker, no marks). Strike plan: on a strike headline plus a fear spike, run the barrels-still-moving check first; if the barrels still move, sell out-of-the-money call spreads at probation size (0.25R shock budget); if the barrels stop, stand down.
